newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks grip gains to end higher.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks grip gains to end higher.

text.p: *Stocks close higher, Q4 inflation figures, options-related trade see early gains held. Volume 345.70 million, value A$717.93 million, 1,117 stocks traded, 342 steady, 398 up, 377 down.

The Australian share market kept a firm grip on its gains to close higher on Wednesday with options-related trade ahead of Thursday's January expiry and well-received inflation data underpinning the rise.
At 4.10 p.m. (0510 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was up 10.0 points at 2,414.2.
March share price index futures were 12 points higher at 2,406, an 8.2 point discount to the index.
While the fourth quarter inflation numbers were right on market expectations, brokers said the figures painted a picture of continuing low inflation, which heartened traders.
"It was basically on expectations," said dealer Nick Atkinson of Brisbane-based brokerage, Wilson HTM, adding while the Dow was down, the market had largely ignored the negatives.
"Our market is looking for the positives," he said, pointing to a relatively strong gold sector which finished barely a whisker lower, despite a sharply weaker bullion price.
"You would have thought gold would have weighed on the market today but it has been a fantastic performance."
The big banks impressed before profit-taking set in. Westpac shares were the pick with several traders suggesting its strength came from a options playa ahead of Thursday's expiry.
Rises slightly shaded falls, while 31 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade boomed ahead of the looming January series expiry. Futures trade was also substantial.
Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 7,369 (10,474)

In other local markets, the Australian dollar tumbled to 10-month lows as a benign inflation report stoked market speculation of an imminent easing in interest rates. The risk of narrowing yield differentials spooked offshore investors who dumped the dollar through its August trough of US$0.7680.
By 4.50 p.m. (0540 GMT), the unit had sunk to US$0.7669/74, it lowest local finish since March 1996, from an early US$0.7684/89 and US$0.7730/35 late Tuesday.

Australian bonds erased their opening gains, with 10-years closing down on day after the long end of the market was sold down when fourth quarter inflation numbers came in right on market expectations.
By 4.50 p.m. (0550 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.47 percent, up on Tuesday's 7.45 percent closing levels.
